message.content:
**Allele frequency of rs7412 (C allele) in Europeans**

| Source | Population | Frequency (C allele) |
|--------|------------|-----------------------|
| **gnomAD v2.1.1** (Exome Aggregation Consortium) | Non-Finnish European (NFE) | **~0.13** |
| **gnomAD v3.1.1** (Genome Aggregation Database) | NFE | **~0.12–0.14** |
| **1000 Genomes Project** (Phase 3) | CEU (Utah residents with Northern and Western European ancestry) | **~0.11** |
| **1000 Genomes Project** | TSI (Toscani in Italy) | **~0.15** |

> **Interpretation:**  
> The C allele at rs7412 defines the ε2 allele of the APOE gene. Across European populations, the ε2 allele frequency typically ranges from ~10 % to ~15 %. The exact value depends on the specific subpopulation and the dataset used.

---

### How to interpret the numbers

* **Allele frequency** = proportion of all copies of the gene in the population that carry the allele.  
  * For example, a frequency of 0.13 means that 13 % of all APOE alleles in that group are the C allele at rs7412.  
* **Population substructure** matters: frequencies can differ between Northern, Southern, Eastern, and Western European groups.  

---

### Quick reference

| Dataset | Sample size | Frequency (C allele) |
|---------|-------------|----------------------|
| gnomAD v2.1.1 (NFE) | ~60 000 exomes | ~0.13 |
| gnomAD v3.1.1 (NFE) | ~125 000 genomes | ~0.12–0.14 |
| 1000 Genomes CEU | 379 individuals | ~0.11 |
| 1000 Genomes TSI | 267 individuals | ~0.15 |

---

#### Bottom line

In most European datasets, the rs7412 C allele occurs in roughly **12 %–15 %** of chromosomes. If you need a more precise figure for a particular subpopulation or study cohort, consult the latest release of gnomAD or the 1000 Genomes Project for that specific group.
